Schools, universities and employers now describe artificial intelligence (AI) literacy in several published frameworks. This section shows how the chapters of this book connect to four of them. It is written mainly for instructors, program designers and accreditation reviewers, but students can use it too: it shows that the skills in this book match what educators in many countries have agreed matters.

## How the Mapping Was Made {.unnumbered}

Every chapter lists four to six learning objectives. Each objective is tagged with one of the book's seven learning outcomes (LO1–LO7) and with up to three framework elements that the objective genuinely develops. The table below collects those tags. It records only what the chapters claim for themselves; nothing was added for this page. A chapter that is missing from a row may still touch that idea, but does not make it a learning objective.

## The Four Frameworks {.unnumbered}

**UNESCO AI Competency Framework for Students (2024).** The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) describes four dimensions (human-centred mindset, ethics of AI, AI techniques and applications, and AI system design) at three progression levels: Understand, Apply and Create (UNESCO, 2024). The book's tags give the dimension and the level.

**AI Fluency Framework, version 1.1 (Dakan & Feller, 2025).** It describes three ways of working with AI (automation, augmentation and agency) and four competencies, often called the 4D: Delegation, Description, Discernment and Diligence. The book keeps these four names in their original English form. Chapter 5 explains why the framework's "agency" is not the same as an AI "agent".

**AI4K12 Five Big Ideas (Touretzky et al., 2019).** Written for kindergarten through grade 12 (K–12), it names five big ideas: Perception, Representation and Reasoning, Learning, Natural Interaction, and Societal Impact. Only a few chapters tag it, because the book's objectives focus on use and judgment rather than on how AI systems are built.

**OECD–European Commission AI Literacy Framework (AILit, 2026).** The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the European Commission published the final version in 2026, after a review draft in May 2025 (OECD/European Union, 2026). Written for primary and secondary education, it groups its competences into four domains: Engage with AI, Create with AI, Manage AI and Shape AI. This edition's objectives were tagged while AILit was still a review draft, so no chapter carries an AILit tag yet; tags will be added in the next edition. As a reading rather than a tag, the closest links are Engage with AI with Part I, and Manage AI, which concerns dividing work between people and AI, with the Delegation Ladder in Chapters 5, 12 and 14.

One more framework appears in two chapters: Long and Magerko's (2020) AI literacy competencies, tagged at the theme "how AI works" in Chapters 4 and 8.

## The Mapping {.unnumbered}

Chapter numbers are those of the chapters whose learning objectives carry the tag. Chapters 6, 13 and 17 are Deep chapters.

| Framework | Element | Chapters that tag it |
|---|---|---|
| UNESCO (2024) | Human-centred mindset | Understand: 1, 7, 8, 10 · Apply: 5, 7, 9, 11, 16, 17, 18, 20 · Create: 20 |
| UNESCO (2024) | Ethics of AI | Understand: 4, 8, 10, 16, 17, 18, 19, 21 · Apply: 1, 7, 9–21 · Create: 21 |
| UNESCO (2024) | AI techniques and applications | Understand: 1–4, 6, 12–15, 17 · Apply: 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 16, 17 · Create: 6 |
| UNESCO (2024) | AI system design | Apply: 6 · Create: 14, 15, 19 |
| AI Fluency 4D (v1.1) | Delegation | 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14, 19, 21 |
| AI Fluency 4D (v1.1) | Description | 1, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| AI Fluency 4D (v1.1) | Discernment | 1–20 |
| AI Fluency 4D (v1.1) | Diligence | 1, 4–21 |
| AI4K12 | Perception | 13 |
| AI4K12 | Representation and Reasoning | 3 |
| AI4K12 | Learning | 2, 3 |
| AI4K12 | Natural Interaction | Not tagged |
| AI4K12 | Societal Impact | Not tagged |
| AILit (2026) | Engage with AI · Create with AI · Manage AI · Shape AI | Not yet tagged (see above) |

Two patterns stand out. Discernment and Diligence, judging outputs and taking responsibility for their use, run through almost every chapter; that is the AI Work Loop's Verify, Decide and Disclose steps at work. AI system design at the Create level appears late, in Chapters 14, 15 and 19, where you design a workflow for your own field.
